The up counter is a synchronous binary counter.
INTRODUCTIONM
With 4 flip-flops, any modulus up to 16 is available.
FREE RUN - In the free run mode of operation, the counter continually counts. For example: The counter starts at 0000, counts to 1111 and starts over again.
SINGLE STEP - In the single step mode of operation, the counter starts counting at 0000 and counts to the maximum count, then stops.

INCREMENTS - Increment is the act of increasing or adding to a quantity or value. For example: Incrementing the number 5 to 6 is increasing 5 by one. To increment the binary number 0011 to 0100 is increasing 0011 by one.

Up counters count in one of two modes of operation. Lets discuss each mode.
In free run mode, the counter counts up to the maximum count allowed by the counter and then starts over.
FREE RUN - This is a MOD 8 counter, the maximum binary count is 0111.
Each input pulse is counted and stored. The count continues up to the modulus.

At the maximum count, all of the inputs to the AND gate have been satisfied (are true) driving the output to a high, thus resetting the counter. The counter will resume counting up with each clock pulse..
In single step mode, the counter counts to the maximum count allowed and stops.
Each input pulse is counted and stored. The count continues up to the modulus.
At the maximum count, the input pulses are disabled inside the counter. The counter stops counting.
What mode of operation is used?

In the free run mode, the counter increments to its maximum count and starts counting over. For example: The counter starts counting at 000, counts to 111, resets to 000 and counts to 111, this process is repeated indefinitely.
TRY AGAIN!
This is a MOD 8 counter, but the mode is either free run or single step.
TRY AGAIN!
What mode of operation is used?
In the single step mode, the counter increments to its maximum count and stops. For example: The counter starts counting at 0000, it counts to 1001 and stops.
TRY AGAIN!
This is a MOD 10 counter, but the mode is either free run or single step.

This counter circuit can count in free run or single step modes in various MODs. It can also be made to operate in various
MOD's, as will be shown later in this lesson.
FreeRun mode of operation is accomplished by placing S2 in the FR position.
With 0000 in the counter, the output of the AND gate is low.
A low applied to the enable input allows the counter to count.
The low is also applied to the D input of the flip-flop.
On the leading edge of the first input pulse, the flip-flop resets producing a high output to the load input.
This disables the load input and the counter starts to count up.
Once the counter reaches the count of 1111, the output of the AND gate becomes high.
The high output of the AND gate stops the counting.
A high is applied to the flip-flop. However, it does not set because the leading edge of the clock is gone.
On the next clock pulse, the flip-flop sets, producing a low to the load input.
Inputs A through D override the pulse input on the clock and set the counter to 0000.
With 0000 in the counter, the output of the AND gate is again low. The counter can now count.
Remember, any MOD can be selected by inverting inputs to the AND gate. This is a MOD 10 counter.
Definition
Instead of using 1010 as the binary count to set the counter to 0000, 1001 is used because of the flip-flop....................
Also remember, inputs A through D do not have to be grounded. This counter counts from binary 0011 to 1001 and back to 0011.
Single Step mode of operation is accomplished by placing S2 to the SS position.
With the count of 0000, a low is applied to the enable input and the counter counts.
The flip-flop has a ground on its input and the output will always be high. This disables the load input.
The counter counts until the count of 1111. Then the output of the AND gate goes high.
The high to the enable input stops the counting.
The flip-flop still has a grounded input. The load input is still high.
The counter does not start counting until S1 is pressed.
Pressing S1 applies a low to the load input which loads 0000 into the counter.
With 0000 in the counter, the counting starts again when S1 is released.
In the single step mode of operation, the counter must be manually restarted.
What is the binary count after the next input pulse?
0000 would be the count if inputs A through D were 0's. The high output of the AND gate enables the LOAD input through the flip-flop.
TRY AGAIN!
1111 would be the count if S2 was connected to ground. This would make the counter single step.
TRY AGAIN!
What is the binary count after the next input pulse?
0000 would be the count if inputs A through D were 0's and if S2 is in the free run position.
TRY AGAIN!
0011 would be the binary count if S2 is in the free run position.
TRY AGAIN!
